questionText: What is the smallest element of a digital image called?
explanation: A digital image is represented in groups of bits called pixels, and a pixel is the smallest element of an image. A layer is a Photoshop editing level, not the smallest part of the image.

questionText: What is the graphic layout that sequences illustrations to tell a story visually before a multimedia product is made?
explanation: A storyboard is a graphic layout that sequences illustrations and images to tell a story visually, used by film makers and video creators as a planning strategy. A histogram shows tones in an image.

questionText: In what unit is image resolution typically described?
explanation: Image resolution is typically described in Pixels per Inch (PPI), how many pixels are displayed per inch of an image; higher PPI gives a crisper image.

questionText: Which Photoshop tool removes unwanted outer areas of an image?
explanation: The Crop tool cuts out or removes unwanted areas of an image. The Eyedropper samples colors and the Hand tool moves the view when zoomed in.

questionText: Which Photoshop tool samples the colors of an image?
explanation: The Eyedropper samples the colors of an image, and a bigger Sample Size gives a better representation of the area's color. The Lasso makes freehand selections.

questionText: Which Photoshop tool lightens the area of the image you paint over?
explanation: The Dodge tool lightens an area of the image you paint over; Burn and Sponge are its optional tools. Burn has the opposite effect of darkening.

questionText: Which tool lets you make freehand selections around an object in Photoshop?
explanation: The Lasso tool allows freehand selections around an object and includes the Polygonal and Magnetic Lasso tools. The Pen draws accurate paths and shapes.

questionText: Which keyboard shortcut duplicates a layer in Photoshop?
explanation: To duplicate a layer you can right-click the layer and choose Duplicate or press Ctrl + J, as used when fixing underexposed photos.

questionText: What is the empty work area of a new Photoshop document, full of pixels you can change, called?
explanation: A new project opens on the workspace, called the canvas, which is full of pixels you can change. The toolbar holds the main editing tools.

questionText: What kind of image is Photoshop mainly designed to work on?
options: Raster images made up of pixels
correctAnswer: Raster images made up of pixels
explanation: Photoshop is a general-purpose application designed to work on any raster-based image, made up of dots or pixels; it also offers some vector graphics features, so 'only vector' is wrong.

questionText: What causes the red-eye effect in photographs?
options: The flash sits right above the lens
The photo was taken outdoors in bright sun
The image has too few pixels per inch
The colors in the photo are too saturated
correctAnswer: The flash sits right above the lens
explanation: The digital camera flash is located right above the lens, which causes red-eye; it can be fixed with the Red Eye tool. Too much saturation makes colors look unnatural, not red eyes.

questionText: Under which tool's button is the Red Eye tool found in Photoshop?
explanation: The Red Eye tool is one of the additional tools of the Spot Healing Brush, along with the Healing Brush, Patch and Content-Aware Move. Clone Stamp has the Pattern Stamp as its extra tool.

questionText: A photo taken indoors without a flash is underexposed and dark. How is it fixed in Photoshop?
options: Duplicate the layer and raise its Exposure
Paint over the dark areas with the Red Eye tool
Use the Clone Stamp in Darken mode
Apply the Blur tool to the whole image
correctAnswer: Duplicate the layer and raise its Exposure
explanation: Pictures taken indoors without a flash turn out underexposed and dark; you duplicate the layer (Ctrl + J) and use Image, Adjustments, Exposure to lighten it. The Clone Stamp in Darken mode is for hot spots caused by a flash.

questionText: Why is the Clone Stamp's blend mode set to Darken when removing hot spots?
options: Only pixels lighter than the sample area are changed
All pixels in the image become darker evenly
The original layer is protected from any change
The sample area is copied without any blending
correctAnswer: Only pixels lighter than the sample area are changed
explanation: Hot spots are light-colored pixels; with Darken mode, Photoshop only changes pixels lighter than the sampled clean area, so the shiny spot darkens gradually.

questionText: Which key is held while clicking to set the Clone Stamp's reference point?
explanation: You hold down the Alt key and click on a clean area to set the reference point or sample; the cursor changes to an eye-dropper. Holding Alt with the Zoom tool zooms out.

questionText: In a Levels adjustment, what are the darkest parts of an image called?
explanation: Every image has shadows (the darkest parts), highlights (the brightest parts) and midtones (everything in between). Hue is a color property, not a tone range.

questionText: Why is an adjustment layer called non-destructive editing?
options: It does not change the original image itself
It keeps a full copy of the image on disk
It cannot be removed once it is applied
It changes only the colors that are clipped
correctAnswer: It does not change the original image itself
explanation: An adjustment layer is non-destructive because it does not change anything about the original image, so you can keep tweaking it or turn it off to compare.

questionText: A histogram in the Levels panel shows a big gap with no information on its right side. What does this mean?
options: The image has a red-eye problem
explanation: A big gap on the right side of the histogram, where highlights are, means the image is underexposed; dragging the white slider left to the histogram's edge fixes it.

questionText: What happens when saturation is removed from an image completely?
options: It becomes a black-and-white or grayscale image
Its colors become very bright and vivid
It becomes underexposed and much darker
correctAnswer: It becomes a black-and-white or grayscale image
explanation: Increasing saturation makes colors vivid and reducing it makes them less vivid; removing it completely produces a black-and-white or grayscale image.

questionText: How does image sharpening make a photo look crisp?
options: It increases the contrast along the edges of objects
It increases the number of pixels in the image
It removes the shadows from the whole image
It lowers the saturation of all colors
correctAnswer: It increases the contrast along the edges of objects
explanation: Sharpening enhances the edges of objects by increasing the contrast of the edges, bringing more definition to details; too much can make the image look worse.

questionText: Which Photoshop tool restores part of an image to an earlier state?
explanation: The History Brush restores part of an image to an earlier state and has the Art History Brush as an extra tool. The Spot Healing Brush removes blemishes.

questionText: What does digital image processing start with?
options: Importing the image from a scanner or camera
Printing the image so that it can be checked by hand
Sharpening the image with the Unsharp Mask filter
Saving the image in a folder under Documents
correctAnswer: Importing the image from a scanner or camera
explanation: Digital image processing starts with importing, capturing the image through a scanner or digital camera, then analysis and manipulation in software, then output to a printer or monitor.

questionText: Which Unsharp Mask setting controls the size of the details that are sharpened, and is best kept very low?
explanation: Radius controls the size of the details sharpened and is best set low, about 0.3 to 0.5 for most images. Amount sets how much sharpness is applied, and Threshold ignores some parts to reduce noise.

questionText: Why is the Unsharp Mask Threshold setting usually kept at 0?
options: Parts of the image may sharpen inconsistently
Raising it removes all colors from the image
Raising it makes the radius too large to control
Raising it converts the layer into a smart object
correctAnswer: Parts of the image may sharpen inconsistently
explanation: Increasing the threshold reduces visible noise by ignoring certain parts of the image, but different parts may then not be sharpened consistently, so it is kept at 0 unless sharpening creates a lot of noise.

questionText: What advantage does Smart Sharpen have over Unsharp Mask?
options: It works only on vector shapes
explanation: Smart Sharpen has noise reduction, which the Unsharp Mask lacks, to reduce the noise that comes with sharpening; it still uses an Amount and a Radius of around 1 or 2.

questionText: When sharpening with the High Pass filter, which blend mode gives stronger sharpening than Soft Light?
explanation: The two most common blend modes for High Pass sharpening are Overlay, which gives higher contrast and stronger sharpening, and Soft Light, which gives more subtle sharpening.

questionText: Why is the background layer converted to a smart object before using the High Pass filter?
options: So sharpening leaves the original image unharmed
So the image turns gray before the filter is selected
So the radius can be set above 5 without clipping
So the layer can be duplicated with Ctrl + J
correctAnswer: So sharpening leaves the original image unharmed
explanation: Converting the layer to a smart object means the High Pass sharpening is applied to the smart object as a smart filter, leaving the original image unharmed.

questionText: When cropping to a specific size with Width 8 and Height 10, what happens to the cropping border?
options: It is constrained so the selected area fits an 8x10 photo
It is fixed at exactly 8 by 10 pixels on the screen
It is removed and the image is cropped automatically
It can be dragged freely to any shape you like
correctAnswer: It is constrained so the selected area fits an 8x10 photo
explanation: With Width and Height specified, the cropping border is constrained: whatever size you drag it, the area within it keeps the 8x10 proportion so it fits on an 8x10 photo.

questionText: How does the Curves tool compare with Levels?
options: It controls shadows, highlights and midtones separately
It can only make an image brighter, never darker
It changes the image size as well as its tones
It is a simpler tool meant for beginners
correctAnswer: It controls shadows, highlights and midtones separately
explanation: Curves is similar to Levels but gives more power to control shadows, highlights and midtones separately; being more advanced, it must be used carefully.

questionText: How is contrast increased with the Curves tool?
options: Drag the curve down in the shadows and up in the highlights
Drag the curve up in the shadows and down in the highlights
Move the two corner points toward the middle
Delete every point on the curve except the corners
correctAnswer: Drag the curve down in the shadows and up in the highlights
explanation: To increase contrast, drag the curve down in the shadows on the left to darken them and up in the highlights on the right to brighten them; the opposite decreases contrast.
